A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V3 reports original alignment experiments in Table 1 and Figures 4–6, with additional DPO, reverse-fine-tuning and scaling experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains original alignment experiments and reports additional algorithm comparisons and KL-divergence results in Appendix B, Figure 7 and Tables 2–3.

M1.justification: The token-tree pruning and Huffman-coding procedure and the forward/inverse alignment framework retain their components. Additional alignment algorithms serve as experimental variants; no new proposed architecture, loss or algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Alpaca, TruthfulQA, Beavertails and IMDb, retaining the instruction, truthfulness, safety and sentiment-generation tasks. The added KL and algorithm experiments change evaluation procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: V3 evaluates SFT and DPO alignment alternatives. V4 adds a four-algorithm comparison on Llama2-7B/IMDb in Figure 7, evaluating PPO, KTO and SimPO alongside DPO. This substantially expands the alignment methods compared experimentally.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces finer snapshot comparisons extending through theta6 and KL-based evaluation. The new rebound protocol measures unsafe examples required to reduce KL divergence below 0.01. V4 also removes the Qwen1.5-72B setting and the DPO pre-training-volume sweep; retained main experiments keep their stated settings.

E4.justification: V4 adds resistance checks across finer snapshots, distribution-level rebound checks and broader algorithm ablations. It removes v3's DPO pre-training-volume analysis and 72B validation. The reverse-direction, DPO model-size and early pre-training-volume analyses are retained, partly under different figure numbers.

E5.justification: Both versions describe shaded standard deviations across positive-data-volume settings in Figures 5–6. Neither reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests, and the new tables and heatmaps introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained plotted series are unchanged, but v4 adds algorithm scores and Tables 2–3. For example, Table 3 reports 961 versus 729 unsafe examples needed for Llama2-7B to reach KL below 0.01 after 1000 versus 10000 safe examples. V3's DPO-volume and 72B result entries are removed.

T1.justification: The normalized rate changes from log M minus gamma to gamma minus log M. The central theorem changes from two positive derivatives to a negative D1 derivative and positive D2 derivative, with a corresponding negative proportionality factor. Appendix A substantially revises the proof, corrects the entropy lemma's logarithm term and removes the earlier large-alpha-and-c assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims: elasticity produces resistance and rebound, depends inversely on dataset sizes, and strengthens with model size and pre-training volume. Additional evidence and mathematical revisions do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V4 interprets perturbations as decreasing D1's normalized rate while increasing D2's, replacing the earlier two-rate increase, and restricts the spring analogy to magnitudes. New Appendix C discusses transfer-learning explanations, data-balancing mitigation and mixed-feature limitations, and tentatively infers an unresolved 0.1–0.5T onset range from retained plots.

D1.justification: V4 adds a first-page code and model-weight availability statement with project-site access information, absent in v3. It also explicitly identifies Qwen1.5 for the retained DPO model-size analysis. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementations.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work, v4 expands positioning around alignment faking and deception, citing Greenblatt, Lang and Park. Appendix C.1 newly contrasts elasticity with transfer-learning accounts, supported by Weiss, Zhuang and Murphy, and argues that existing accounts cannot fully explain the phenomenon.

P1.justification: Related work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, the binary-token assumption moves into the appendix, and experimental material is regrouped into B.1–B.3. Exposition, broader-impact paragraphs and author/contact text receive localized rewrites, while the abstract and most of the original main narrative remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V4 redesigns Figures 1–2 and 5–6, including annotations, colors, axes and captions; adds two tables and an algorithm heatmap; and removes the DPO-volume and 72B plots. Retained v3 Figures 7 and 9 become v4 Figures 9 and 8, respectively.

improvement.justification: The new KL tests provide more direct evidence of distributional return than v3's task-score proxies, and broader algorithm checks strengthen empirical support. The normalization now agrees with the stated smaller-is-better interpretation, and resource access is documented. These gains are limited by lightly specified KL procedures, unclear parameter conditions in the revised proof, and removal of the 72B and DPO-volume evidence.
